newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG's higher despite inventory data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG's higher despite inventory data.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were mostly higher Thursday, despite industry data showing near-record July propane builds, players said.

Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane was traded slightly higher at 36.28 and 36.50 cents a gallon, despite Wednesday's Energy Information Administration data that showed July inventories increased by 7.1 million barrels.

Players suspected speculation by large trading companies was driving the market. "The inventory numbers tell us this kind of market shouldn't be happening, but it is," one trader said. "Bigger players are making deals in hope of turning up the market and making money."
Back month Beliveu propane deals were also higher. January material was heard done at 38.00 and February at 37.00 cents.
Conway, Kansas, propane was quiet. Material values were pegged slightly higher at 35.50/36.00 cents. December propane there was heard done at 37.00 cents.
The only other Conway deal heard done was butane at 41.50 cents.
"There's not much buying interest in the Midwest," said one trader.
Belvieu ethane was done at 21.75 and ethane mix at 20.75.
